families.name: Fruity
families.examples: Start with fresh or dried fruit. Try citrus, orchard fruit, berries or dried fruit; use lemon, apple or raisin only if that memory fits.

families.name: Floral
families.examples: Think of a flower you know. Blossom, rose or violet may help; simply floral is enough if a particular flower is unfamiliar.

families.name: Herbal
families.examples: Try fresh green herbs, dried herbs or leafy impressions. Mint is one familiar reference, not the answer to every green aroma.

families.name: Spicy
families.examples: Think of a spice cupboard: cinnamon, clove or pepper. An aromatic spice association does not mean the wine tastes hot.

families.name: Toasty
families.examples: Consider toasted bread, roasted coffee or cocoa. These words describe associations; they do not establish a particular barrel recipe.

families.name: Earthy / savoury
families.examples: Try mushroom, dried leaves or another familiar savoury association. An earthy word is not proof that soil has passed into the wine.

samples.name: Lemon peel
samples.prepare: Wash a lemon and place a small piece of fresh peel in a clean glass. Smell from above the rim; compare it with your memory of citrus.
samples.reflection: Did it feel broadly fruity, then citrus-like? Lemon and other citrus memories can overlap.

samples.name: Fresh apple
samples.prepare: Put a freshly cut slice of an apple you know in a clean glass. Smell it now, then again later and notice whether it changes.
samples.reflection: Was orchard fruit useful even if the apple variety was hard to name? Freshness and variety change the reference.

samples.name: Raisins
samples.prepare: Put a few plain raisins in a clean glass. Smell them separately from the fresh apple. Use familiar dried fruit if raisins are unavailable, but record the actual substitution.
samples.reflection: Did dried fruit fit better than fresh fruit? Your own familiar dried-fruit word is useful too.

samples.name: Fresh mint
samples.prepare: Lightly bruise a clean mint leaf in a glass. Smell gently; compare the leafy impression with any more specific association.
samples.reflection: Did herbal fit? Mint can be particularly distinctive, and does not stand for every herb.

samples.name: Cinnamon stick
samples.prepare: Place a plain cinnamon stick in a clean glass. Smell gently without grinding it or inhaling powder.
samples.reflection: Could you describe it as spicy before naming cinnamon? Familiarity with a spice changes how easily its name comes to mind.

samples.name: Plain toast
samples.prepare: Let a small piece of plain toasted bread cool, then place it in a clean glass. Compare its smell with untoasted bread if available.
samples.reflection: Was toasted or roasted enough? Toast level and the bread itself change what you notice.
